title: Exhibition: "Hidden Layers: AI Infrastructures and Hallucinations"
location: Worth Ryder Art Gallery, Anthropology & Art Building, Rm 116
description: The Department of German and the Department of Art Practice are excited to announce the opening of Hidden Layers: AI Infrastructures and Hallucinations, curated by Antonio Somaini with Hannes Bajohr, Sonja Thiel and Elena Yu, in dialogue with the France–Berkeley research initiative The Latent Spaces of Culture, and on display at the Worth Ryder Art Gallery. In neural networks, the "hidden layers" are the intermediate strata of transformation between input and output — the computational structures where data are transformed, weighted, and recombined into increasingly abstract, distributed representations that no human eye can read. The exhibition Hidden Layers: AI Infrastructures and Hallucinations takes this term as its conceptual frame, bringing together seventeen international artists and researchers working at the intersection of contemporary art and machine learning to make visible what artificial intelligence keeps out of sight: its planetary infrastructures and computational latent spaces, its colonial and ideological underpinnings, its misrecognitions and hallucinations, and its transformation of our relation to the past through the silent reprocessing of pre-existing cultural forms. The exhibition is organized in four sections: "In the Latent Spaces of Culture," "Material Infrastructures," "Colonial Imaginaries: From Misrecognition to Generative Slopaganda," and "Hallucinations and Psychedelia." Featuring works by Nouf Aljowaysir (https://www.noufaljowaysir.com/); Gašper and Nina Beguš & Metahaven (https://latentspacecraft.antikythera.org/); Grégory Chatonsky (https://chatonsky.net/); Kate Crawford & Vladan Joler (https://anatomyof.ai/); Asma Kazmi (https://www.asmakazmi.com/) & Jill Miller (https://www.jillmiller.net/); Andrea Kh��ra (https://www.andreakhora.com/); Occitane Lacurie & Barnabé Sauvage (https://www.schirn.de/en/schirnmag/3-questions-for-occitane-lacurie-und-barnabe-sauvage/); Greg Niemeyer (https://www.gregniemeyer.com/); and Mario Santamaria (https://mariosantamaria.net/) & Alex Saum-Pascual (https://www.alexsaum.com/).Hidden Layers is a collaboration between the Department of German and the Worth Ryder Art Gallery at the Department of Art Practice. It is part of the France–Berkeley research initiative The Latent Spaces of Culture: a collaboration between UC Berkeley, the Université Sorbonne Nouvelle in Paris, and the French National Center for Scientific Research (CNRS).Exhibition Dates: September 3 - October 3, 2026Opening Reception (https://events.berkeley.edu/art/event/323504-exhibition-opening-reception-hidden-layers-ai-infrast): Thursday, September 3, 4-6:30pm, Worth Ryder Art Gallery Open to the public,RSVP (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd_OOMe7YQHw3CYbSr673UCSlQ0f4mn4lZ7g46KhRUTRpC5qQ/viewform) requestedArtist Talk, Gregory Chatonsky "INFRALLUCINATION" (https://events.berkeley.edu/art/event/324432-artist-talk-grgory-chatonsky-infrallucination): Thursday, September 3, 6:30-8:00pm, AAPB 285 Open to the public,RSVP (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd_OOMe7YQHw3CYbSr673UCSlQ0f4mn4lZ7g46KhRUTRpC5qQ/viewform)required (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd_OOMe7YQHw3CYbSr673UCSlQ0f4mn4lZ7g46KhRUTRpC5qQ/viewform)Film Program, Push Buttons and AI (https://bampfa.org/event/push-buttons-and-ai): September 9, 7 pm, BAMPFA RSVP (https://bampfa.org/event/push-buttons-and-ai)Curatorial Tour, led by Antonio Somaini (https://events.berkeley.edu/livewhale/?events_edit&id=328238): Friday, September 11, 4:30pm, Worth Ryder Art Gallery Open to the public, no RSVP requiredWorkshop on Latent Space of Culture: September 10, 2pm-4pm; September 11/12, 9:30 am-4pm on both days, 470 StephensBerkeley AI Futures Salon (https://bids.berkeley.edu/berkeley-ai-futures-salon): On the Subject of Art in Artificial Intelligence: September 16, 6:30pm– 9pm Apply to attend (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSenC1GtID5I8JrILQqwW3cL4sFhgbc3BagB6aoh10Q1WK8aQA/viewform)Water and AI. Times subject to change, please also check the campus calendar (https://events.berkeley.edu/art). This exhibition is supported by the France-Berkeley Fund of the Institute of European Studies, the Department of German and the Department of Art Practice, together with the Berkeley Center for New Media, the Berkeley Institute for Data Science (BIDS), Department of Rhetoric; Antikythera, the Human Technology Futures (HTF), the Pamela P. Fong and Family Distinguished Chair in China Studies, the Division of Arts & Humanities, the Townsend Center for the Humanities, the School of Information, the Technology Network of the Berkeley Economy and Society Initiative (BESI), and the Berkeley Art, Law, and Finance Project, hosted by the Berkeley Center for Law and Business at Berkeley Law.  In conjunction with the exhibition, additional programming is developed in collaboration with Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive (BAMPFA), San Jose State University, and the Institute for Contemporary Art San Jose.

title: All-Campus Virtual OSPO Meetup
description:
This month UC Santa Cruz hosts and the topic is mentorship as community building: how mentoring and peer mentorship help build and sustain open source communities. We'll hear about UC Santa Cruz's Open Source Research Experience (OSRE) and peer-mentorship programs, including how participants go on to become mentors themselves and build capacity even when faculty can't mentor directly. Speakers: Stephanie Lieggi and Hari Kuttivelil (OSRE mentoring), and Emily Lovell and Silas Morgan (peer mentorship). The second half is an open community call for network updates, project sharing, and general OSS chat.

Students, staff, faculty, researchers, and folks outside UC all welcome!
Register here: https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/98527182449?pwd=PMdoVaOTSYuAHqPVWQbYPGHOmGrb5o.1

title: OSPO All-Campus Virtual Meetup: September
location: Zoom
description: Join us in shaping the future of open source at UC Berkeley, building on its rich legacy of leadership in open source software development! At our monthly live online discussion and knowledge exchanges, we can harness the collective intelligence and creativity of our community to meaningfully transform how research is conducted, produced, and disseminated. Visit (https://bids.berkeley.edu/programs-initiatives/open-source-program-office-ospo)the OSPO page (https://bids.berkeley.edu/programs-initiatives/open-source-program-office-ospo) for more OSPO info and events.

The exhibition Hidden Layers: AI Infrastructures and Hallucinations takes this term as its conceptual frame, bringing together seventeen international artists and researchers working at the intersection of contemporary art and machine learning to make visible what artificial intelligence keeps out of sight: its planetary infrastructures and computational latent spaces, its colonial and ideological underpinnings, its misrecognitions and hallucinations, and its transformation of our relation to the past through the silent reprocessing of pre-existing cultural forms. The exhibition is organized in four sections: "In the Latent Spaces of Culture," "Material Infrastructures," "Colonial Imaginaries: From Misrecognition to Generative Slopaganda," and "Hallucinations and Psychedelia." Featuring works by Nouf Aljowaysir (https://www.noufaljowaysir.com/); Gašper and Nina Beguš & Metahaven (https://latentspacecraft.antikythera.org/); Grégory Chatonsky (https://chatonsky.net/); Kate Crawford & Vladan Joler (https://anatomyof.ai/); Asma Kazmi (https://www.asmakazmi.com/) & Jill Miller (https://www.jillmiller.net/); Andrea Kh��ra (https://www.andreakhora.com/); Occitane Lacurie & Barnabé Sauvage (https://www.schirn.de/en/schirnmag/3-questions-for-occitane-lacurie-und-barnabe-sauvage/); Greg Niemeyer (https://www.gregniemeyer.com/); and Mario Santamaria (https://mariosantamaria.net/) & Alex Saum-Pascual (https://www.alexsaum.com/).Hidden Layers is a collaboration between the Department of German and the Worth Ryder Art Gallery at the Department of Art Practice. It is part of the France–Berkeley research initiative The Latent Spaces of Culture: a collaboration between UC Berkeley, the Université Sorbonne Nouvelle in Paris, and the French National Center for Scientific Research (CNRS).Exhibition Dates: September 3 - October 3, 2026Opening Reception (https://events.berkeley.edu/art/event/323504-exhibition-opening-reception-hidden-layers-ai-infrast): Thursday, September 3, 4-6:30pm, Worth Ryder Art Gallery Open to the public,RSVP (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd_OOMe7YQHw3CYbSr673UCSlQ0f4mn4lZ7g46KhRUTRpC5qQ/viewform) requestedArtist Talk, Gregory Chatonsky "INFRALLUCINATION" (https://events.berkeley.edu/art/event/324432-artist-talk-grgory-chatonsky-infrallucination): Thursday, September 3, 6:30-8:00pm, AAPB 285 Open to the public,RSVP (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd_OOMe7YQHw3CYbSr673UCSlQ0f4mn4lZ7g46KhRUTRpC5qQ/viewform)required (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd_OOMe7YQHw3CYbSr673UCSlQ0f4mn4lZ7g46KhRUTRpC5qQ/viewform)Film Program, Push Buttons and AI (https://bampfa.org/event/push-buttons-and-ai): September 9, 7 pm, BAMPFA RSVP (https://bampfa.org/event/push-buttons-and-ai)Curatorial Tour, led by Antonio Somaini (https://events.berkeley.edu/livewhale/?events_edit&id=328238): Friday, September 11, 4:30pm, Worth Ryder Art Gallery Open to the public, no RSVP requiredWorkshop on Latent Space of Culture: September 10, 2pm-4pm; September 11/12, 9:30 am-4pm on both days, 470 StephensBerkeley AI Futures Salon (https://bids.berkeley.edu/berkeley-ai-futures-salon): On the Subject of Art in Artificial Intelligence: September 16, 6:30pm– 9pm Apply to attend (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSenC1GtID5I8JrILQqwW3cL4sFhgbc3BagB6aoh10Q1WK8aQA/viewform)Water and AI. Fong and Family Distinguished Chair in China Studies, the Division of Arts & Humanities, the Townsend Center for the Humanities, the School of Information, the Technology Network of the Berkeley Economy and Society Initiative (BESI), and the Berkeley Art, Law, and Finance Project, hosted by the Berkeley Center for Law and Business at Berkeley Law.  In conjunction with the exhibition, additional programming is developed in collaboration with Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive (BAMPFA), San Jose State University, and the Institute for Contemporary Art San Jose.

The exhibition Hidden Layers: AI Infrastructures and Hallucinations takes this term as its conceptual frame, bringing together seventeen international artists and researchers working at the intersection of contemporary art and machine learning to make visible what artificial intelligence keeps out of sight: its planetary infrastructures and computational latent spaces, its colonial and ideological underpinnings, its misrecognitions and hallucinations, and its transformation of our relation to the past through the silent reprocessing of pre-existing cultural forms. The exhibition is organized in four sections: "In the Latent Spaces of Culture," "Material Infrastructures," "Colonial Imaginaries: From Misrecognition to Generative Slopaganda," and "Hallucinations and Psychedelia." Featuring works by Nouf Aljowaysir (https://www.noufaljowaysir.com/); Gašper and Nina Beguš & Metahaven (https://latentspacecraft.antikythera.org/); Grégory Chatonsky (https://chatonsky.net/); Kate Crawford & Vladan Joler (https://anatomyof.ai/); Asma Kazmi (https://www.asmakazmi.com/) & Jill Miller (https://www.jillmiller.net/); Andrea Kh��ra (https://www.andreakhora.com/); Occitane Lacurie & Barnabé Sauvage (https://www.schirn.de/en/schirnmag/3-questions-for-occitane-lacurie-und-barnabe-sauvage/); Greg Niemeyer (https://www.gregniemeyer.com/); and Mario Santamaria (https://mariosantamaria.net/) & Alex Saum-Pascual (https://www.alexsaum.com/).Hidden Layers is a collaboration between the Department of German and the Worth Ryder Art Gallery at the Department of Art Practice. It is part of the France–Berkeley research initiative The Latent Spaces of Culture: a collaboration between UC Berkeley, the Université Sorbonne Nouvelle in Paris, and the French National Center for Scientific Research (CNRS).Exhibition Dates: September 3 - October 3, 2026Opening Reception (https://events.berkeley.edu/art/event/323504-exhibition-opening-reception-hidden-layers-ai-infrast): Thursday, September 3, 4-6:30pm, Worth Ryder Art Gallery Open to the public,RSVP (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd_OOMe7YQHw3CYbSr673UCSlQ0f4mn4lZ7g46KhRUTRpC5qQ/viewform) requestedArtist Talk, Gregory Chatonsky "INFRALLUCINATION" (https://events.berkeley.edu/art/event/324432-artist-talk-grgory-chatonsky-infrallucination): Thursday, September 3, 6:30-8:00pm, AAPB 285 Open to the public,RSVP (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd_OOMe7YQHw3CYbSr673UCSlQ0f4mn4lZ7g46KhRUTRpC5qQ/viewform)required (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd_OOMe7YQHw3CYbSr673UCSlQ0f4mn4lZ7g46KhRUTRpC5qQ/viewform)Film Program, Push Buttons and AI (https://bampfa.org/event/push-buttons-and-ai): September 9, 7 pm, BAMPFA RSVP (https://bampfa.org/event/push-buttons-and-ai)Curatorial Tour, led by Antonio Somaini (https://events.berkeley.edu/livewhale/?events_edit&id=328238): Friday, September 11, 4:30pm, Worth Ryder Art Gallery Open to the public, no RSVP requiredWorkshop on Latent Space of Culture: September 10, 2pm-4pm; September 11/12, 9:30 am-4pm on both days, 470 StephensBerkeley AI Futures Salon (https://bids.berkeley.edu/berkeley-ai-futures-salon): On the Subject of Art in Artificial Intelligence: September 16, 6:30pm– 9pm Apply to attend (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSenC1GtID5I8JrILQqwW3cL4sFhgbc3BagB6aoh10Q1WK8aQA/viewform)Water and AI. title: Git and GitHub Webinar
description:
The CURIOSS Sharable OSPO Working Group is running a hands-on Git & GitHub webinar on Tuesday, September 15, 10am-12pm PT / 1-3pm ET!

It's a concept-first, beginner-friendly session: we'll open your first pull request into a shared repo, walk through what's actually happening with branches and commits, and work entirely in the browser (no installs). Great for students and anyone who wants to get comfortable collaborating on GitHub.

Register here: https://www.eventbrite.ie/e/git-and-github-webinar-tickets-1998342861292

Open to everyone across (and beyond) the UC system. Hope to see you there!

title: Exhibition: "Hidden Layers: AI Infrastructures and Hallucinations"
location: Worth Ryder Art Gallery, Anthropology & Art Building, Rm 116
description: The Department of German and the Department of Art Practice are excited to announce the opening of Hidden Layers: AI Infrastructures and Hallucinations, curated by Antonio Somaini with Hannes Bajohr, Sonja Thiel and Elena Yu, in dialogue with the France–Berkeley research initiative The Latent Spaces of Culture, and on display at the Worth Ryder Art Gallery. In neural networks, the "hidden layers" are the intermediate strata of transformation between input and output — the computational structures where data are transformed, weighted, and recombined into increasingly abstract, distributed representations that no human eye can read. The exhibition Hidden Layers: AI Infrastructures and Hallucinations takes this term as its conceptual frame, bringing together seventeen international artists and researchers working at the intersection of contemporary art and machine learning to make visible what artificial intelligence keeps out of sight: its planetary infrastructures and computational latent spaces, its colonial and ideological underpinnings, its misrecognitions and hallucinations, and its transformation of our relation to the past through the silent reprocessing of pre-existing cultural forms. The exhibition is organized in four sections: "In the Latent Spaces of Culture," "Material Infrastructures," "Colonial Imaginaries: From Misrecognition to Generative Slopaganda," and "Hallucinations and Psychedelia." title: UC Carpentries: Core Elements of Citable and Discoverable Research Software
description:
Learn practical steps for making research software citable, discoverable, and reusable. Working in your browser with a GitHub repository, you will add an open-source license, create a CITATION.cff file, make a versioned release with a DOI and improve project documentation and metadata. This hands-on workshop is designed for researchers and the professionals who support them.

This event is co-presented by the UC OSPO Network and UC Carpentries.

This workshop is free and participants can register for individual topics or the entire series. View the complete schedule and register.

The UC OSPO Network Alignment Group Alignment Group brings together the chairs and delegates of the Network's Working Groups to coordinate cross-cutting work and keep the groups aligned as the Network's governance takes shape. title: Office Hours (Thursdays)
description:
We'd love to see you at our coworking sessions! These are casual, drop-in-if-feel-like it sessions where you can: 

- Ask questions relating to OSS, your campus OSPO, or the OSPO network
- Get help finding a project to work on, or getting more contributors for your own project

title: All-Campus Virtual OSPO Meetup
description:
A monthly gathering for the UC open source community. Each meetup is co-hosted by a different campus in the network—the hosting campus sets the agenda for the first half (demos, workshops, guest speakers, whatever they want to share), and the second half is an open community call for network updates, project sharing, and Q&A.
Students, staff, faculty, researchers, and folks outside UC all welcome!
Register here: https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/98527182449?pwd=PMdoVaOTSYuAHqPVWQbYPGHOmGrb5o.1

descriptionHtml: The Department of German and the Department of Art Practice are excited to announce the opening of Hidden Layers: AI Infrastructures and Hallucinations, curated by Antonio Somaini with Hannes Bajohr, Sonja Thiel and Elena Yu, in dialogue with the France–Berkeley research initiative The Latent Spaces of Culture, and on display at the Worth Ryder Art Gallery.  In neural networks, the "hidden layers" are the intermediate strata of transformation between input and output — the computational structures where data are transformed, weighted, and recombined into increasingly abstract, distributed representations that no human eye can read. The exhibition Hidden Layers: AI Infrastructures and Hallucinations takes this term as its conceptual frame, bringing together seventeen international artists and researchers working at the intersection of contemporary art and machine learning to make visible what artificial intelligence keeps out of sight: its planetary infrastructures and computational latent spaces, its colonial and ideological underpinnings, its misrecognitions and hallucinations, and its transformation of our relation to the past through the silent reprocessing of pre-existing cultural forms. The exhibition is organized in four sections: "In the Latent Spaces of Culture," "Material Infrastructures," "Colonial Imaginaries: From Misrecognition to Generative Slopaganda," and "Hallucinations and Psychedelia." title: UCLA Open Source Meetup: Keeping the World on Time
location: Charles E. Young Research Library, Data Science Center, Room 11630L
description:
Join colleagues from UCLA and across the University of California for a hybrid lunch-hour conversation with UCLA Computer Science Teaching Professor Paul Eggert, primary coordinator of the public-domain Time Zone Database (TZDB) and a longtime contributor to GNU software projects.

TZDB does far more than keep the clocks on our phones and computers accurate. It supports timestamps on documents and photographs, preserves historical time-zone information used by software, and must respond when governments change their clocks with little warning.

In “Keeping the World on Time: Inside the Time Zone Database,” Eggert will introduce this widely used but largely invisible infrastructure and discuss the technical, legal, political and collaborative challenges involved in sustaining it. The program will feature a 30–40-minute talk followed by an extended Q&A and conversation with the audience.

In-person attendance is limited to 16 seats, and advance registration is required. Bring your own lunch; light refreshments and beverages will be provided. Online participation will also be available to members of the wider UC community.

Featured Speaker: Prof. Paul Eggert

Paul Eggert is the primary coordinator of the public-domain Time Zone Database (TZDB), which coordinates timestamps on computing devices worldwide, and a copy of which surely resides on your smartphone. He designed TZDB's naming standard and continues to manage its data and code amid technical, legal, and political challenges. Over the years he has also contributed to core free software projects, including the GNU C Compiler, C Library, Coreutils, Diffutils, Gnulib, and Emacs, and in 2022 he was given the Free Software Foundation Award for the Advancement of Free Software. After a career in the software industry that included positions at the world's first independent computer software company, the world's then-second largest computer company, and startups, he joined the UCLA Computer Science Department, where he is now a Teaching Professor.

Who Should Attend?

This event is open to students, faculty, staff, researchers, librarians and technologists from UCLA and across the UC system. All experience levels are welcome, from people curious about open source to active contributors and project maintainers.

Hosted by the UCLA OSPO in partnership with the UC Open Source Program Office (OSPO) Network.

Learn More About the Time Zone Database

For an accessible introduction to Eggert and his work, read the UCLA Samueli profile “Time Zone King: How One UCLA Computer Scientist Keeps Digital Clocks Ticking.” You can also visit the official IANA Time Zone Database website or explore the TZDB source code and project documentation on GitHub.

Bring your lunch and join the conversation. Light refreshments and beverages will be provided.

The UC OSPO Network Alignment Group Alignment Group brings together the chairs and delegates of the Network's Working Groups to coordinate cross-cutting work and keep the groups aligned as the Network's governance takes shape. Meetings are open to anyone in the UC open source community. Working-group delegates are asked to attend, and everyone else is welcome to join and listen in. Learn more at ucospo.net.
